A1.justification: Both PDFs describe UniSim and provide readable text, equations, figures, tables, and appendices A–F. All 18 pages of each version were inspected; the appendices are unchanged.

before.justification: v3 reports original evaluations on peptides, small molecules, proteins, and alanine-dipeptide, plus ablations and inference-efficiency measurements in Appendix E.

after.justification: v4 retains those empirical results and adds a pretraining ablation through the UniSim/p results in Table 1.

M1.justification: Section 4.4 revises the reported protein-adaptation workflow: v3 finetunes the existing vector-field model, whereas v4 initializes from pretrained atomic-representation weights and trains the vector field and guidance kernel on ATLAS. The general architecture, losses, and inference procedure remain unchanged.

E1.justification: The pretraining sources and evaluated molecular coverage are retained: PepMD, MD17/MD22, ATLAS, and alanine-dipeptide. The new pretraining ablation introduces no additional dataset, domain, or test scenario.

E2.justification: Table 1 adds UniSim/p as an internal comparator without pretraining. External comparator membership is unchanged: FBM, Timewarp, ITO, and SD on PepMD; FBM, ITO, and SD on ATLAS. Timewarp's ATLAS exclusion is newly explained, not newly imposed.

E3.justification: The stated ATLAS initialization/training configuration changes from vector-field finetuning to training from pretrained atomic representations. Table 1 also introduces a control without pretraining. Retained splits and metrics are unchanged; the PDFs do not establish whether ATLAS experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: Section 4.2 and Table 1 add a direct comparison of vector-field models with and without pretraining. This is distinct from the retained atomic-embedding-expansion ablation in Table 9. Other sensitivity analyses, force-guidance ablations, and case studies are retained.

E5.justification: Mean/std reporting across test molecules is retained, including for the new Table 1 row. Table 8 still specifies averaging three independent runs per peptide. No seed, run-count, confidence-interval, or significance-testing practice changes.

E6.justification: Table 1 adds six UniSim/p results. Its mean PWD distance is 0.400 and validity is 0.332, versus 0.332 and 0.505 for UniSim/g; TIC slightly favors UniSim/p, 0.503 versus 0.510. Previously reported numerical rows remain unchanged, and Figure 5 retains the same plotted evidence.

T1.justification: The equations, formal assumptions, Proposition 3.1, and Appendix B proof are unchanged. Equation 24 is newly called heuristic, but its formula and the formal mathematical content are retained.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction's contribution list, and conclusion retain the same claims about unified cross-domain simulation, molecular pretraining, stochastic interpolants, and force guidance. The added ablation supports an existing contribution.

C2.justification: v4 explicitly qualifies the force-guidance loss as heuristic and attributes pretraining benefits to the new UniSim/g–UniSim/p comparison instead of the comparison with FBM. Section 4.4 reframes the protein experiment around scalability. Existing validity and long-trajectory limitations remain.

D1.justification: v4 removes the ATLAS-specific learning rate of 1e-4 and Figure 5's specification of the first 200 generated conformations. It newly explains Timewarp's atomic-velocity requirement. Appendix disclosures covering code access, preprocessing, hyperparameters, refinement, and hardware are unchanged.

R1.justification: Section 3.4 explicitly attributes inspiration for the heuristic loss to Wang et al. (2024a), refining the connection to an already cited work. The cited-work set, bibliography, and related-work survey are unchanged.

P1.justification: Several method and experimental paragraphs are rewritten to clarify training descriptions, comparator coverage, and interpretation of the ablation. Section order and the overall narrative remain intact; the abstract, introduction, conclusion, and appendices are retained.

P2.justification: Table 1 gains a UniSim/p row and corresponding formatting adjustments. Figure 5 is re-exported with the same visible data, while its caption drops the first-200-conformations qualifier. Text and displays reflow locally; appendix layouts are unchanged.

improvement.justification: The new direct pretraining control strengthens attribution of several benefits beyond v3's comparison with FBM. Explicitly labeling the loss heuristic and correcting the baseline-coverage explanation also improve precision. These gains are limited by removing the ATLAS learning rate and Figure 5 sample scope, and by leaving the revised ATLAS training description unreconciled with unchanged scores.
